newsitem.title: FRANCE: Annan sees better U.N. relations with Iraq.
newsitem.headline: Annan sees better U.N. relations with Iraq.

text.p: U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan said on Friday that Iraq's relations with the United Nations were improving and he intended to work personally to that end.
On an official visit to Paris, Annan said he would meet Iraqi Deputy Prime Minister Tareq Aziz in New York within two weeks.

"Relations are improving. Obviously, there is still the question of disarmament and the work of the Ekeus commission. We have had some difficult moments, but I think things are moving forward," he said after talks with French Foreign Minister Herve de Charette.
"So I plan to work personally and to involve myself very much in this issue," Annan said.
Iraq is still subject to U.N. economic sanctions imposed after its 1990 invasion of Kuwait, which have remained in force following the 1991 Gulf War.

The world body agreed in December to allow Baghdad for the first time to sell a limited amount of oil in exchange for food and medicine for its civilian population. The oil sales began last month but none of the food has yet been distributed.

Iraqi Oil Minister Amir Muhammad Rasheed said earlier on Friday that Iraq was holding talks with the United Nations on increasing the income from the oil for food deal, limited to $2 billion over six months under U.N. resolution 986.
He said Annan was preparing a report that would suggest an increase in the money permitted from oil sales.
Annan did not refer directly to the issue in his remarks and U.N. officials were not immediately available to comment on Rasheed's statement, made at a news conference in Baghdad.
Some 30 percent of Iraq's oil money goes to a U.N. fund to compensate victims of the invasion of Kuwait. Iraq has also to meet other U.N. costs.
Iraqi Foreign Minister Mohammed Saeed al-Sahaf was in New York on Friday and was expected to ask the head of the U.N. Humanitarian Affairs Department for increased income from the oil-for-food deal.

France pressed Aziz when he visited Paris last month to comply fully with the disarmament commission headed by Rolf Ekeus of Sweden, which is mandated to supervise and verify the elmination of Iraq's weapons of mass destruction.
